title: db engine creation: bare postgresql:// URIs are pinned to the psycopg2 driver before the engine is built
answers: Why does my MLflow server fail with 'No module named psycopg' after upgrading SQLAlchemy to 2.1 with a postgresql:// backend store URI?
How do I make a PostgreSQL tracking or backend URI use psycopg2 explicitly, or use psycopg3?
Where is the PostgreSQL driver chosen for a tracking, registry, or auth database URI?
Where does the auth database upgrade command create its engine from a PostgreSQL URL?
body:
Path: Tracking, model-registry and auth database URIs (backend-store-uri, tracking URI for a PostgreSQL server) are turned into SQLAlchemy engines in mlflow/store/db/utils.py:create_sqlalchemy_engine; the auth `upgrade` command in mlflow/server/auth/db/cli.py:upgrade calls create_engine directly.
Rule: A bare `postgresql://` scheme is rewritten to `postgresql+psycopg2://` before sqlalchemy.create_engine is called, so the driver no longer depends on the SQLAlchemy default (2.1 defaults to psycopg3). Any new direct create_engine call on a PostgreSQL URL must apply the same normalization, as mlflow/server/auth/db/cli.py:upgrade now does.
Symptom: After SQLAlchemy 2.1 was installed, starting a server or store with a bare postgresql:// backend or tracking URI failed at engine creation with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'psycopg'.
Constraints: Applies only to PostgreSQL URLs; SQLite and MySQL URLs are untouched, and an explicit +psycopg2 or +psycopg scheme is the user's choice. Do not add this rewrite to the fs2db migrate path (mlflow/store/fs2db/__init__.py:migrate): that path only accepts SQLite targets and registers a SQLite-only PRAGMA listener, so a PostgreSQL rewrite there is unreachable.
applies: Any code that turns a user-supplied database URI into a SQLAlchemy engine for MLflow's SQL stores; not for SQLite or MySQL URIs.
says: Tracking server crashes on startup when configured with a standard PostgreSQL database address.
Starting the server with a PostgreSQL backend fails with missing database driver errors.
The database upgrade command for authentication fails when pointing to a PostgreSQL database.
Allow standard PostgreSQL connection strings to work without requiring explicit driver prefixes.
search: When creating SQLAlchemy engines for tracking, model registry, and auth stores in mlflow/store/db/utils.py:create_sqlalchemy_engine and mlflow/server/auth/db/cli.py:upgrade, bare postgresql:// URIs are rewritten to postgresql+psycopg2:// before calling sqlalchemy.create_engine. This prevents engine creation failures with ModuleNotFoundError for 'psycopg' caused by SQLAlchemy 2.1 defaulting bare postgresql:// schemes to psycopg3. This normalization applies strictly to PostgreSQL database URIs while leaving SQLite, MySQL, and explicit driver schemes untouched, and must not be added to the SQLite-only fs2db migration path.
